items.stem: After ingestion, answers about one PDF type are always wrong or empty. The most likely root cause is:

options.text: Text extraction silently failed for that PDF type, so no content was indexed
options.rationale: Correct: failed extraction leaves empty units, so retrieval has nothing to find.

options.text: The language model is too small
options.rationale: The content was never indexed; model size is not the cause.

options.text: The user's question is too polite
options.rationale: Phrasing does not explain systematically empty content.

options.text: The vector store is too fast
options.rationale: Speed is unrelated to missing extracted text.

items.explanation: Correct: failed extraction leaves empty units, so retrieval has nothing to find.

items.stem: Which TWO metadata fields best support later citation and traceability? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: a source identifier lets an answer point back to its origin.
Correct: a section reference supports precise, checkable citation.

options.text: A random UUID with no mapping to the source
options.rationale: An unmapped id does not aid tracing to the real source.

items.explanation: Correct: a source identifier lets an answer point back to its origin.

options.text: Loss of structure that hurts chunking and retrieval relevance
options.rationale: Correct: meaningful structure aids chunking and retrieval; destroying it degrades quality.
Removing useful structure does not improve answers.
Structure loss measurably affects downstream stages.
Citation depends on preserved structure and metadata, not its removal.
